title: Hand-eye mouse control
summary: Good aim is driven by visual feedback, fine motor control, and adaptable mouse control rather than memorizing one exact force-distance pairing forever.
cues: Treat the mouse like an extension of the hand guided by visual feedback
Judge aiming skill by how well the crosshair is placed, not by preserving one sacred setup
Expect skilled players to adapt quickly to small setup and sensitivity changes
failureModes: Explaining every performance dip as broken muscle memory
Ignoring how pad wear, skates, humidity, and friction already force constant adaptation
